txt: The shed follows the clock: afternoon, golden, sunset, dusk, night - and overcast when the clouds close in.
The explode button pulls the aeroplane apart, part from part.
Wing loading is the weight over the wing area: a trainer near 40 kg/m², an ultralight under 25.
Every new aeroplane is registered F-PGAR until you letter your own.
The camera pills: 3/4 front, side, plan, nose, and the pilot’s own eyes.
The procedural world the game was built on, still one pick away in the graphics menu.
Bench check, wing loading, density altitude, test flight: the tests that earn the plaque, and the logbook under them.
The room is lit by the same sky as the island: the hour you pick in the shed is the hour you fly in.
Both are drawn on the aeroplane. The centre of gravity must sit ahead of the neutral point: the gap between them is the stability margin.
The switches work: M the master, K the beacon, N the navigation lights, T the taxi light, I the instruments.
A garage build out on the concrete. The time of day, the clouds and the wind are yours to set.
The island is Annette Island, Alaska, from its real elevation data. The map names every field you can land on.
Forest, muskeg, heath and rock: the ground is read from the island's own land-cover maps.
Floats are a gear choice in the garage. The sea and the lakes are runways too.
C cycles the views: chase, orbit, cockpit, wing and tower.
After dark the windows light up and the piers keep their lamps on.
